idiom_name: net/http handler function per route (Go 1.22 method patterns)
implementation_notes: net/http already realizes the action/responder pair: mux.HandleFunc("GET /users/{id}", h) registers exactly one handler per method and path (Go 1.22 patterns), the handler collects input with r.PathValue and query parsing, and the responder role is the http.ResponseWriter plus an encoder (json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(v)) or http.ServeFile. The Action and Responder classes are unnecessary - the function per route plus the writer replaces them - and the domain must stay a plain function or interface that never receives *http.Request. Introduce a separate responder type only when one action must serve several representations or when shared response building is worth testing on its own.
pitfalls: A header written after the first body byte is silently ignored; set Content-Type and status before encoding the body.
Handlers must be safe for concurrent use: request state kept in a captured variable instead of r.Context() is a data race.
Passing *http.Request or http.ResponseWriter into the domain re-couples business logic to HTTP and makes it untestable without a server.
